satis

adverb; also an indeclinable noun with a genitive, and with esse, “to be enough”

With a genitive, enough of: negōtī satis, enough to do; with esse, “is enough”: semel satis est, once is enough (Cic. Att. 13.52.2). More than enough: satis superque (Catull. 7.2), or plūs satis (Ter. Eun. 85). Lewis & Short: satis is enough so that nothing more is needed, affatim so that nothing more is wanted.

Other words

  • sat — enough (the short form)

    adverb and indeclinable noun · also used · classical · Plaut. Aul. 3.6.24: pol vel legiōnī sat est (Lewis & Short); Cic. Sen. 48: tantum quantum sat est (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx plērumque poētica et cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; rarer in prose (Lewis & Short))

  • affatim — plenty, as much as one wants

    adverb · also used · classical · Plaut. Poen. 3.1.31: edās dē aliēnō quantum velīs, ūsque adfatim (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short: enough so that one wishes for no more; satis is enough so that one needs no more.

  • satis superque — more than enough, enough and to spare

    also used · classical · Cic. ND 2.2: contrā Epicūrum satis superque dictum est (Lewis & Short s.v. contrā); Hor. Epod. 1.31: satis superque mē benignitās tua ditāvit (Lewis & Short s.v. benignitās); Traupman 115; Traupman 310

    Traupman writes sat superque; the classical authors write satis.

Examples

  • Satis est.

    That’s enough.composed

  • vēscere, sōdēs. — jam satis est. — at tū, quantum vīs, tolle. — benignē

    Do eat, please. — I’ve had enough. — Well, take as much as you like. — No, thank you.Hor. Ep. 1.7.15–16

  • semel satis est

    once is enoughCic. Att. 13.52.2

  • quaeris, quot mihi bāsiātiōnēs tuae, Lesbia, sint satis superque

    you ask, Lesbia, how many of your kisses would be enough and more than enough for meCatull. 7.1–2

  • claudite ōstia, virginēs: lūsimus satis

    shut the doors, girls: we have played enoughCatull. 61.224–225

  • aestāte puerī sī valent, satis discunt

    in summer, if children are well, they learn enoughMart. 10.62.12

  • satis ēloquentiae, sapientiae parum

    eloquence enough, too little wisdomSall. Cat. 5.4

  • accēde ad ignem hunc; jam calēscēs plūs satis

    come to this fire; you’ll soon be more than warm enoughTer. Eun. 84–85

  • satis temporis

    enough timeTraupman 310

  • Sat est.

    That’ll do.Traupman 393

See also again, that’s enough!, too little, too, more.
